comments.text:
The separation of Jamaica and Cayman in 1962 was slightly more nuanced.  Jamaica had a socialist government in 1962.  Grand Cayman had a number of socialist politicians and narrowly Grand Cayman voted to stay with Jamaica - significant divisions existed within the population though, many not wanting to end up part of a socialist state.  However, Grand Cayman reversed its position when the two smaller sister islands declared that if Grand Cayman decided to remain with Jamaica, they would cede from the Cayman Islands and remain a British territory. All politicians then agreed that the islands must stay together - thus potential disaster was averted.  
Cayman is not free from poverty and yes, there are many wealthy people in Cayman.  The good thing is that the poor do get taken care of with a national health insurance provider and housing support. Unemployment is low because companies must have a 50%+ Cayman workforce and the government civil service effectively hires anyone else that can’t get a job elsewhere.  It’s not perfect - but we are self sufficient and run a budget surplus. And compared to Jamaica, crime is very low.

comments.author: @BrentDuty
comments.text:
It’s pronounced Kay-man, Kay-man’-yen. 

The original Caymanians were mariners, they made their living off the sea. They harvested turtles and sailed to South America for produce and anything they needed. They also harvested the mahogany forest on the island. 

They built and sailed schooners and invented a cat boat unique to Cayman. Caymanian men learned to navigate and become mariners. My great great grandfather founded the first navigation mariner school in Cayman and passed on his knowledge to future captains. The islands have the deepest waters and sounds as well as sheltered reefs to protect ships from bad weather. 
Caymanians didn’t just sail the Caribbean, they sailed around the world. My great great uncle Robert Creighton was a famous sailor of the Three Bells and saved an American ship’s passengers.

My ancestry goes back to the beginning of the island’s story. The thing most of you all don’t see is the culture of Cayman is their resilience. Caymanians use humility, courage, honor, respect, laughter as currency. They are inventive  and keen to risk taking behavior. Cayman is a place where the art of stopping time in the form of story telling lives. It’s the secret hidden in plain site.
